name: Direct-to-chip liquid cooling (cold plates and CDUs)
principle: Cold plates mounted on CPUs and GPUs carry coolant to a coolant distribution unit (CDU) that rejects the heat to facility water or room air, decoupling the server loop from the building loop. Air cooling tops out around 40 to 60 kW per rack with containment; liquid cooling carries AI-class racks of 80 kW to 120 kW and beyond. The Vertiv CoolChip family spans 70 kW to 2.3 MW per unit with liquid-to-air and liquid-to-liquid exchangers, redundant pumps, integrated filtration and leak detection.

advantages: Carries AI-class rack densities that air containment cannot
Liquid-to-air CDUs retrofit into existing halls
Precise loop control reduces thermal shock to CPUs/GPUs
limitations: Requires server-level plumbing, quick disconnects and coolant chemistry management
Facility-water models need plant changes; leak detection is mandatory for production
Standards for coolants and connections are still consolidating
